requirements.requirement: Serve a usable package repository from node1's local storage.
requirements.summary: The executor created a local repository containing the tree RPM and generated metadata, configured HTTP serving, and directly retrieved repomd.xml over node1's managed address. After reboot, Apache was active, port 80 was listening, metadata returned HTTP 200, and the repository still advertised the package.

requirements.requirement: Make the usual remote repositories unavailable to package installation.
requirements.summary: BaseOS, AppStream, and Extras were disabled before installation, and alma-local was the only enabled repository. The installation transaction named alma-local as its source. This demonstrates functional isolation from the usual remote repositories, although it does not demonstrate a network-level outage.

requirements.requirement: Install and run a package from the local repository while the usual remote repositories are unavailable.
requirements.summary: DNF installed tree-1.8.0-10.el9 from alma-local while it was the sole enabled repository. RPM queries and tree --version confirmed the installed, working package both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection dropped during reboot, a different post-restart boot ID was observed, and system, HTTP service, repository metadata, package availability, installed package, and repository isolation all recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.
limitations: Remote-repository unavailability was established by disabling the usual DNF repositories and showing alma-local as the sole enabled source; no network-level blocking or outage was directly tested.
The lifecycle snapshots inventory temporary paths only in a bounded manner, so hygiene conclusions are limited to the captured state.
The single-node topology has no separate cluster state to recover; service, repository data, package state, and system health were directly verified instead.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task-related roles: installing repository prerequisites, creating and serving repository content, configuring repository isolation, installing tree, and executing the mandatory restart. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified. Two small evidence artifacts, /tmp/repomd.pre and /tmp/repomd.post, were left behind rather than cleaned up; this is minor executor-caused residue. Package consistency remained healthy, no failed services appeared, and the new port-80 listener was required for the repository.
